Apply for the UK to join the European Union as a full member as soon as possible, I believe joining the EU would boost the economy, increase global influence, improve collaboration and provide stability & freedom. I believe that Brexit hasn't brought any tangible benefit and there is no future prospect of any, that the UK has changed its mind and that this should be recognised., I think the Single Market would bring inward investment, frictionless trade and economic growth benefiting industry and consumers alike.

Full membership could also amplify the UK’s voice on the global stage, allowing it to influence EU policy and regulations, including trade, security and environment.

Joining the EU could provide access to science & research projects and give UK citizens the right to live, work & study across member states, enhancing cultural exchange & personal opportunities.

Maintain the £3 bus fare cap permanently, As of the budget, we think that working people on lower incomes or who live in rural communities will suffer as a consequence of the decision to raise the bus fare cap to £3. We think bus fares should be permanently capped at £3 after December 2025., If the government wants to prioritise growth and improving the lot of 'working people', we think they should consider this. Buses are a method of transport used by many vulnerable people - the young, the old and those on lower incomes. We feel that allowing the £3 bus fare cap to expire will take money out of the pockets of those who cannot afford it due to the cost of living. People cannot economise their bus use, people need to get to work or school - bus use is a need, not a want.

Legalise use of privately owned e-scooters and e-bikes on public roads, Legalise the use of electric bikes and scooters for use of the public., We believe that use of these items could lower carbon emissions and get people out more. It could save time and money that people might otherwise spend on fossil fuels for simple tasks like going to the shops.
 
Mobility scooters are legal, so we think e-bikes and e-scooters should be too.
 
We believe that the majority of people riding said scooters and bikes are careful around the public.

Legalise adult adoption, We think it is time for adult adoption to be legalised in the UK.

We believe amending this law would offer individuals the opportunity, as a legal adult, to sever connections with absent, abusive, or otherwise unsuitable parents., Places legalising adult adoption include:
- Some US States
- Some Provinces in Canada
- Japan
- Germany
 
The age for adoption ends when the individual reaches 18. Due to this being the cut off age, this doesn't give the individual the independence of being classed as an adult and processing their own adoption application. Applications made prior to the age of 18 are subject to the approval of the named parents, except in specific circumstance.
 
We believe this law is extremely detrimental to the mental health of individuals who have experienced abuse at the hand of their parent(s).

Raise help to buy ISA threshold to up to £350,000 (or up to £550,000 in London), Since help to buy was introduced, property prices have increased. Those who took out a help to buy ISA and haven’t yet used it may be priced out of being able to obtain the government bonus, 25% of the ISA up to £3,000, as the property price threshold has not risen in line with property prices., To assist first time buyers, we think the government should allow use of help to buy ISA’s on property up to £350,000 outside of London, and £550,000 inside London.

Otherwise, many have saved up in a help to buy ISA with the promise of 25% bonus, but won’t be able to use it as average property prices are above the £250,000 threshold.

Stop road tax on zero-emission vehicles (ZEVs) from 2025, We believe that charging road tax on ZEVs risks undermining the UK’s commitment to reducing carbon emissions and reaching our net-zero targets., We think that by keeping road tax at zero for ZEVs, the government could demonstrate bold leadership on climate action, encouraging greater adoption of clean vehicles and affirming the UK’s dedication to a sustainable, green future. We believe that now is the time to prioritize policies that reduce emissions, support green innovation, and solidify the Government's commitment to addressing the climate crisis.

Seek to expel the USA from the UN using Article 6 of the UN Charter, We want the Government to invoke Article 6 to seek to expel the USA from the UN.

Article 6 of the charter allows for any member, including Security Council members, to be expelled for persistent violations of UN principles. Expulsion is decided by the General Assembly after a UNSC recommendation., We believe the USA has persistently violated the principles of the UN Charter, both with & without its veto power, including by vetoing motions relating to Palestine, including calls for an immediate ceasefire.

We believe fundamental UN reform is essential to ensure fair global representation, justice, and peace for all peoples, including but not limited to the people of Palestine. We think expelling the USA from the UN is the first necessary step in this process.

To create buffer zones around schools, stopping intimidation of staff & children, On the 25th March 2024, the Khan Review recommended the creation of a 150m buffer zone around schools to prevent protests happening directly outside of school gates. We think the recommendations should be implemented asap, with allowances for protests at the weekend and outside school hours., We think there have been a number of protests that have caused intimidation of school staff.

Legally Require All Job Listings to Show Salaries Upfront, We ask the Government to make it a legal requirement that all job listings show salary ranges clearly and upfront. We believe this would create a fairer, more transparent job market, better inform candidates and reduce time-wasting when searching for jobs., Sources state that 35% of UK job listings don’t list salaries, wasting time and widening wage gaps in various fields such as marketing (People Managing People, 2023). Countries such as the U.S. (in states like California) and the EU already require salary ranges in job postings (HR Dive, 2023; Council of the EU, 2023). We believe that a UK law would ensure fairer pay practices, reduce disparities, and help candidates make informed choices, building a more efficient and transparent job market.

Ban non-stun slaughter in the UK, In modern society, we believe more consideration needs to be given to animal welfare and how livestock is treated and culled.

We believe non-stun slaughter is barbaric and doesn't fit in with our culture and modern-day values and should be banned, as some EU nations have done., In a landmark case, the European Court of Human Rights has ruled that a ban on the ritual slaughter of animals without prior stunning does not violate the ECHR.

The Court considered that the protection of public morals, to which Article 9 of the Convention referred was not indifferent to the living environment of individuals covered by its protection and including animals.

Fines on companies for carbon emissions can fund renewable energy+sustainability, We urge Parliament to impose fines of 5-15% of annual revenue on corporations based on their carbon emissions,with a 1.5-year grace period.Revenue should fund renewable energy,public transport,and sustainability projects.This initiative will encourage eco-friendly practices and combat climate change, We would like Parliament to impose fines on corporations based on carbon emissions to combat climate change. Many large companies contribute significantly to greenhouse gases but lack incentives to adopt sustainable practices. Fines of 5-15% of their annual revenue will hold them accountable and encourage emission reductions. The revenue generated can be reinvested in renewable energy, public transport, and sustainability projects, promoting a healthier environment and economic growth.

Hold a referendum to decide if the UK should leave the ECHR., We ask the government to arrange a public referendum on the UK’s membership in the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR). This referendum could allow UK citizens to determine if we should continue adhering to the ECHR or establish independent human rights standards., We think that a referendum on the ECHR could give the British public a voice in deciding the UK’s human rights framework. We feel that the ECHR, while established to protect fundamental rights, increasingly influences UK policy and limits our control over key national matters, such as immigration and security. We think an independent framework could enable the UK to craft policies that reflect its unique legal and cultural values, safeguarding both individual rights and national interests in a balanced way.

Make St. David's Day on March the 1st a Public Holiday, I want the Government to declare St. David's Day on March the 1st a Public Holiday.

I think there is sufficient support for this.,

Create path to Settlement for Ukrainians in the UK, We urge the UK government to provide a path to settlement for Ukrainians living in the UK. These individuals face significant uncertainty about their future. We think allowing them to settle would provide the stability needed to rebuild their lives and contribute to British society., We believe Ukrainians in the UK have become valuable members of our communities, and a pathway to settlement would affirm our commitment to supporting those impacted by conflict. We kindly ask for your consideration of this matter.

Enable disabled bus pass users to travel during peak times across England, We call on the Government to change the English National Concessionary Travel Scheme (ENCTS) so disabled bus pass users can use their pass before 09.30 am, and provide the necessary funding to local councils. , Disabled workers tend to be on lower incomes. We are given means to help us get to work but the use of these passes are restricted to off peak in many areas. A lot of start times for jobs are not off peak. We think that the DFT should change the policy and allow the use during peak times.

Increase the Lifetime ISA house price limit in line with inflation , Adjust the Lifetime ISA house price limit to reflect current market values, allowing first-time buyers in high-cost areas access to homes under this program., We think the £450,000 limit, set in 2017, no longer reflects housing affordability. UK house prices have risen by around 25%, with London’s average now around £525,000. We believe many first-time buyers are unable to use the Lifetime ISA to purchase in high-cost areas, limiting access to government assistance for young buyers. We think an updated limit would help bridge the gap in today’s housing market.

Ban wind farms on protected peat land in England, In its recent consultation on new onshore wind planning regulations, the government asked if some habitats, such as those containing peat soils, need extra protection from renewable energy development. We say YES! As did 90% of respondents to this question., We think the unintended consequence of building wind farms on protected peat land would be to worsen the nature and climate crisis - peatland's stored carbon would be released as a result of infrastructure construction. Reliable analysis shows there's plenty of available land in England for all the onshore wind farms needed for the green transition, without building on protected peatland. The Government should apply the precautionary principle - there is nothing to lose by doing so.

Provide grants of £25,000 for independent tackle shops., We urge the Government to make £25,000 digital transformation and viability grants available. We believe this support would protect the heritage and sustainability of these shops as vital cultural and community assets., In our view independent tackle shops are more than retail spaces; they are community hubs that preserve fishing traditions, support conservation, and contribute to mental health and well-being. We think these shops face rising costs and intense competition, risking closure. Without government intervention, we think a vital part of UK heritage may disappear. We think targeted grants could ensure these shops' survival, helping them adapt digitally and continue their contribution to communities and environmental education.

Repeal the Climate Change Act 2008 and Net Zero targets, We consider that Parliament must revoke The Climate Change Act 2008 and related Net Zero targets as since 2008 when The Climate Change Act became law many hundreds of scientists up to the highest Nobel Laureate level have jointly declared "There is no climate emergency"., We believe the Climate Change Act 2008 and related Net Zero targets are both now in effect based on just one side of a two-sided scientific debate as we do not consider there to be a scientific consensus on the hypothesis of human emissions causing climate change. We consider that one side only of a two-sided scientific debate is not an acceptable basis for significant legislation that could have major impacts on the UK's economy and citizens. We want the issue of Climate Change to be reconsidered from scratch based on views and evidence from all sides.

Include Wales in the Union Flag, I urge the Government and Parliament to recognize Wales's integral role within the UK by updating the Union Jack to include Wales. I am calling for an official review and redesign process that engages experts, stakeholders, and the public to ensure Wales's rightful place on our national flag., Currently, the flag incorporates elements of England, Scotland, and Ireland but overlooks the distinct identity and heritage of Wales, despite its status as one of the UK's four nations. I think this change would foster greater inclusivity, accurately reflect the unity of all UK nations, and promote a sense of equal representation and national pride. I am a firm believer that this change would be a positive one for the people of the United Kingdom.

Introduce scheme for reduced or free public transport fares, I believe that there should be a government scheme to make public transport fees reduced or free across the country, in addition to the existing bus fare cap., I think doing so could address climate change, cost of living, and urban accessibility. Public transport can help reduce global emissions, and it has been reported that some cities with free transport see higher ridership and lower congestion. We believe this policy could ease financial strain, improve air quality, create safer streets, and has the potential to lead to a more sustainable and inclusive society.

Vote against the Assisted Dying Bill, I would like MPs to vote against the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill. I believe it sets a dangerous precedent, devaluing life based on contribution, not inherent worth. I think it undermines our core principles & puts doctors in a conflicted position, challenging their oath to protect life., We urge the UK Government to reject the Assisted Dying Bill and instead prioritize initiatives that improve palliative care, mental health support, and resources for those experiencing end-of-life challenges. These alternatives could ensure dignity and support. I believe that relying on implementing assisted dying instead places vulnerable people at risk and does not uphold our societal commitment to valuing life.

Make Saint David's Day (Wales) and Saint George's Day (England) Bank Holidays, I think Dydd Gwyl Dewi (Saint David's Day) on 1st March in Wales and Saint George's Day on 23rd of April in England should be made to be bank holidays. I believe these dates are important for the people of the respected nations, and are a day of celebration that should be open for everyone to enjoy., A national holiday for each nation of the UK is important and can be a day of celebration and reflection, this is something that already happens in Scotland, which celebrates Saint Andrew's day on the 30th of November. I believe it is therefore fitting for Wales and England to follow suit and celebrate their national day with a bank holiday as well.

We are petitioning for a National Referendum on Assisted Dying, We believe that the decision to introduce assisted dying legislation in the UK, is a matter of such fundamental import to the future of our nation and to us as citizens, that it must be decided as a nation, not by Members of Parliament alone., It is also our view that the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill 2024-25, now before Parliament, requires far more scrutiny and time for deliberation than will be afforded by a Private Member’s Bill, as is the case in this instance. In the interests of reaching a rational and reasoned decision on the matter, we believe it is imperative that time is set aside to discuss and reflect upon the economic, political and cultural contexts in which assisted dying legislation would be exercised.

Legally require unanimous jury verdicts for serious offences., We believe majority jury verdicts can lead to miscarriages of justice. , We think majority jury verdicts can risk unsafe convictions, which should always be proved "beyond reasonable doubt". We believe the principle of jury unanimity should be reinstated for indictable only offences.

Review the Highways Act 1980 to allow safe EV charging cables across pavements, We urge the Government to review the Highways Act 1980 to permit the safe use of charging cables across pavements, under specific conditions. These include cables being placed under protectors, laid flat and straight from property to vehicle, and used during periods of low pedestrian traffic., We believe current rules impact people living in urban areas, where off-street parking is rare. We think public charging points are often costly, insufficient, and frequently occupied by non-EV vehicles. We think this creates significant barriers to EV ownership, limiting efforts to meet environmental targets and reduce carbon emissions.

We think this change could enable more people to adopt EVs, make sustainable transport more accessible, and ensure safe, minimally disruptive charging solutions for those without off-street parking.

Reduce salary threshold of 38,700 for visa sponsorship requirements, We call on the Government to review and reduce the £38,700 minimum salary threshold for skilled worker visa sponsorship, as this figure is significantly above typical UK salaries and creates unnecessary barriers for both businesses and skilled migrants., The current threshold:
- Far exceeds the UK median salary (approximately £30,000)
- Creates an artificial barrier for skilled workers in many legitimate professions
- Disproportionately affects small businesses and regions outside London
- May force current visa holders to leave the UK despite being valued employees
- Risks splitting families where the main visa holder cannot meet the new threshold.

This review is crucial for supporting business growth and family unity.

Set limits on the length of lane closures for roadworks, Set limits for roadworks on motorways and A roads including:
- Limiting lane closures to 3 miles maximum on motorways, 1 mile on A roads. 
- No roadworks or lane closures allowed within 20 miles of other works.
- All work areas resourced 24 hours a day in non-residential areas until completion., We believe that continuous lane closure disruption may cause:
- Increased potential for accidents
- Reduced access for emergency vehicles
- Delayed business deliveries
- Difficulty planning journeys
- Increased journey times
- Personal stress
- Road rage
- Lateness for medical appointments, work, school, flights, etc.
- Damage to the environment due to pollution from concentrated stationary traffic

Stop Windsor Post office closure, Windsor Post office is part of historic Windsor, tourists often going there after visiting the castle.  It is a key lifeline for many Windsor residents.  Windsor castle appears on stamps and it is the home to our Royal family.  Closing this Post office without considering other options is a mistake., This is a lifeline for many Windsor residents - there is only one bank open in the whole town 
People come into town to go to the Post office - reducing footfall will add to shop closures and hence is very short sighted 
Reduced numbers of tourists visiting the high st 
There are other options to consider such as Royal support or take over by the local community

Allow driving motorcycles up to 125cc without CBT on category B driving licence, I would like the government to introduce new rules to allow persons with a category B driving license to ride a 125cc Motorbike with no CBT requirement. Similar legislation has been in force in Germany since 2020, and I believe the UK should follow suit., I believe this could help to ease emissions and congestion on the roads. I believe the criteria for this should be the following: 

Driver must be at least 25 years old
Must have held their licence for at least 5 years
They must complete 13.5 hours (nine x 90-minute sessions) of theory and riding practice
After the training is completed, there would be no final test, and the driver is awarded an A1 licence.

Introduce a threshold for the public to call a General Election., To ensure the Government remains accountable to the electorate, a threshold should be introduced to call a General Election by the public. An example could be a 2/3rd majority of the number of voters that voted at the last General Election., This will ensure no Government can be elected on a set of promises and then immediately lie, backtrack and break them. This would restore a sense of trust in politics and give the public the power to call an election if the overwhelming majority were in disagreement and wanted a fresh choice.

Review the UK political system, We think the UK should review the current political and governance model, including how it could allow consideration of longer term change with cross party commitment., We think our historical political behaviours are inappropriate for modern society.

We think there is no long term planning and commitment. We think the needs of the public have become second order to the interests of individuals.  

We think this review should consider abolishing the House of Lords and leaving Westminster for a modern professional environment.
 
We think extremist views are not the answer, but that the public have no choice apart from an ineffective 2 party system.

We believe the only answer is to change the political model for the UK.

Breaking manifesto promises should be illegal and reprimanded as fraudulent., Penalties for breaking manifesto promises within the first 6 months of winning a general election., Broken manifesto promises within the first 6 months should be brought to parliament's attention and action taken against the party that has broken it's promised to the public.

Save the Prince of Wales Theatre and the Museum of Cannock Chase, There is a proposal being tabled on Thursday at Cannock Chase District Council to permanently close both the Prince of Wales Theatre and Museum of Cannock Chase, despite promises of redevelopment as part of the ‘levelling up project’, Step in and stop the closure happening

Abolish the deadline for the purchase of new petrol and diesel cars, We believe that those purchasing new cars should be allowed to exercise complete freedom of choice in making their choice of vehicle. , The deadline for the sale of petrol and diesel cars, along with the zero emission vehicle mandate restricting the proportion of new petrol or diesel cars, should be abolished. We believe the deadline removes freedom of choice from customers and is completely against the principles of a free market. We think that abolishing the deadline on new petrol and diesel cars and the zero emission vehicle mandate, which links the number of ICE cars sold to the number of EV cars, would restore the principle of a free market to the car manufacturing and sales sector. We think it would also restore the incentive for car manufacturers to develop 'low emission' ICE technology.

Introduce IQ minimum for Government and Parliament members, We think the people in charge with passing laws, running the overall country interests should at least have an IQ of over 100 (country average). We think this could help make sure there is efficiency, common sense and productivity amongst the highest institution’s members., This could be a first step towards efficiency in UK. All members of Government and Parliament to be tested for IQ by third party entities. No lower than 90 (below country average) should be allowed to stand.

UK to advocate for freedom of speech and free press in Eritrea, I call on the UK Government to seek to pressure Eritrea to restore freedom of speech and independent media, release imprisoned journalists, and provide greater internet access. I believe the UK must advocate for human rights and support Eritreans in their fight for freedom and justice., Many are concerned basic freedoms, including free speech, press, and communication, being restricted in Eritrea. Independent media has been banned since 2001, and there have been reports of many journalists being jailed without trial. Internet access is heavily restricted, which silencing and isolating millions. The UK values democracy and human rights, and I believe it can use its influence to push for reforms by advocating for press freedom, internet access, and the release of journalists.

Base vehicle excise duty on a combination of mileage and emissions, Why should someone doing 1000 miles per annum pay the same VED as someone doing 100000? The greater the mileage the greater the pollutants and infrastructure wear and tear., We think if the government are serious about reducing pollution this change could penalise those who pollute most and help those who only have a vehicle due to necessity.

Protect Smithfield meat market and Billingsgate fish market from closure., I would like Smithfield and Billingsgate to be made Historic Trading locations with protected status as a meat market and a fish market respectively., Smithfield and Billingsgate have helped shape the fabric of London and deserve to maintain their significance, which comes from their function as marketplaces.

Raise pay for civil servants and standardise pay bands across departments, At the lowest level, some civil service workers are paid close to minimum wage, whilst holding what we feel are major responsibilities over the lives of people, not only in those in their relevant ministries but also the general public. We are advocating for higher, equal wages across all ministries, We think it makes sense for pay bands to be standardised across all government departments. We think it makes no sense that equivalent pay bands across different departments could be getting roughly £6,000 difference, some may earn minimum wage and some may earn comfortable living wages for very similar jobs. Many civil servants enjoy their jobs and serving the government and general public and we believe that their wages should replicate the work that they put in.

Abandon the Assisted Dying Bill and focus on offering superb palliative care, Stop the Assisted Dying Bill!!! By focusing on excellent end-of-life healthcare, we can honor the dignity of those who are dying, providing them with love, comfort, and support in their final days., "Every life matters, especially at its most vulnerable moments. Let’s stand together for compassionate care, not shortcuts. By focusing on excellent end-of-life healthcare, we can honor the dignity of those who are dying, providing them with love, comfort, and support in their final days. Sign the petition to abandon the Assisted Dying Bill and advocate for a healthcare system that values life and offers hope to the very end."

scrap emission ban targets  on vehicles, We the majority wish the government to scrap all emission targets for vehicles including the 2030 target imposed on us, The majority of people do not want electric vehicles, there manufacture causes more environmental harm, and they are to expensive and this policy does nothing to help us or the environment

Referendum - Assisted Suicide / Assisted Dying - A Referendum is required., The UK Parliament does not have the jurisdiction over Christian belief.  Only the full population of the UK have the right to determine who should have assisted dying / assisted suicide and whether it is acceptable by the UK population itself. This should not be left to 400MPs., Simple referendum is needed. It is not urgent for Parliament to make this at this time. The UK needs a full referendum with the benefits and the negatives. It should not be rushed through as otherwise it insults all Abrahamic religions.

Call for a referendum on the UK's pursuance of Carbon Net Zero., Give British citizens the choice, via a referendum ballot, on whether or not we pursue Carbon Net Zero, We are being forced to move over to expensive electric cars with low range, inefficient expensive heat pumps, our countryside being blighted by solar & wind farms, jobs being lost & expensive energy being imported, pushing up energy prices for the British people. We weren't given the choice to go this way, the government are telling us we have to.

Change the threshold for Historic (Classic) vehicles to 25 years or less, The current threshold is 40 years or more. We wish to change this to 25 years. This would be for both the MOT and Tax rules., We believe vehicles are not built to last as long as they used to. We believe 25 years would be more reflective of when cars should be considered as a historic or a classic vehicle.

Launch an inquiry into structural racism experienced by Travellers, We would like the Government to launch an inquiry into structural racism experienced by travellers., We would like consideration to be given to:

Culture Awareness Training
Penalties for hate crimes for both individuals and statutory bodies
Further investment into support for the Traveller Community who experience trauma.

Stop the introduction of blasphemy laws in the uk, Not to introduce any blasphemy law in the United Kingdom., We ask the Government to respect and uphold the principles of freedom and fairness, ensuring that no single group imposes its beliefs on the majority. The strength of a pluralistic society lies in its ability to accommodate a multitude of voices and perspectives while maintaining respect for individual rights and freedoms.

Require there to be general election to replace a Prime Minister, We call upon the UK Government to introduce and pass legislation that makes it illegal for any political party to remove or replace an elected Prime Minister without a General Election., We believe that re-electing a Prime Minister without the consent of the people undermines the very principle of democracy, and we believe this can create a situation where political elites, rather than the public, decide who leads the country.
We think this creates a precedent for ignoring the public's wishes and could diminish the legitimacy of political decisions and government actions.

The UK does NOT need a blasphemy law, We urge the UK Government to reject any proposals to reintroduce blasphemy laws. These laws restrict free speech, privilege specific religions, and harm social cohesion. Existing hate speech laws already protect individuals from harm without curbing the right to question or criticise beliefs., Reintroducing blasphemy laws would undermine free speech, a cornerstone of democracy, by penalising the critique of religious beliefs. Such laws historically caused inequality, privileging some faiths while marginalising others. They would also create fear, stifling debate, art, and academia. Existing hate speech laws ensure protections without limiting expression. The UK must champion open dialogue and equality, not regress to laws that threaten liberty and fairness.

Make GCSE Science an optional subject, I think that GCSE Science should be made an optional subject. I think that students should not be forced to take science as a subject. , If not made optional, students who fail GCSE science should be forced to resit it, bringing it in line with the requirements for GCSE English and Maths which are both also mandatory subjects.

Cap of £10,000 per individual donor to political parties, Currently anyone can give an unlimited amount to political parties. The cross-party Committee on Standards in Public Life has recommended a cap of £10,000 per individual donor., We think the £10,000 cap should be implemented to prevent billionaires buying influence in British politics & undermining our political institutions & democracy.

Reconsider the closure of London’s oldest meat and fish markets., The potential closure of Smithfield and Billingsgate Markets threatens not only the livelihoods of countless traders but also the preservation of an essential part of London’s heritage, economy, and identity., To ensure the survival of Smithfield and Billingsgate Markets, I call on the government to take decisive action to preserve these historic and economically vital institutions. These markets are more than just places of trade—they are integral to London’s identity, economy, and community life. Their closure would represent a failure to protect the nation’s heritage and small businesses.

Ban cross-examination of victims of sexual abuse, We think banning cross-examination of victims of sexual abuse in court would be right and be fair to the victims of these dreadful crimes. Victims should be heard, it takes courage to stand up and speak out. We think cross examination is cruel and unfair on victims of these dreadful crimes, We think this ban would make it fairer and easier for victims of these terrible crimes to be able to come forward, to be able to have their voice heard. Victims should not be scared of justice but should be able to trust justice, without worrying about being judged through cross examination. Victims of these terrible crimes have had enough trauma then may end up having more trauma, from the system that is supposed to listen and care and protect.

Call A Referendum on Net-Zero, Give the people of the UK a referendum on whether we should continue Net Zero or stop the whole Net Zero project, The Net Zero project has been pushed by politicians from all the major parties, it is time to give the people of the UK the chance to decide if the effort and cost is worth it

Introduce a written UK constitution, with protections like US first amendment., I believe the UK should introduce a written constitution, with protections like the US first amendment. I think any law that infringes these should be annulled., The protections would be:
Parliament shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion, or prohibiting the free exercise thereof; or abridging the freedom of speech, or of the press; or the right of the people peaceably to assemble, and to petition the Government for a redress of grievances.

Make private flyers pay for their Carbon emissions, UK Government must legislate to:
*Tax jet fuel
*Increase other taxes & duties on planes with few passengers
*Require fuel for outbound flights to be bought in the UK to avoid tax evasion and curb carbon emissions
*Require private jets to carbon offset , From Jan‘22-Oct‘23, private jets of 200 of the world's richest people emitted the same amount of carbon as almost 40,000 Britons. In 2022 alone they made 27793 flights - just 0.5% of the 5.3m private flights that year, while public airlines formed only 7% of UK emissions. Right now jet fuel isn’t taxed at all but we think it could raise billions in tax income to improve people’s lives.

We think this data show the disproportionate impact of the privileged few. We believe the government need to act to bring an end to this.

Introduce a new rule for MPs to take an oath to adhere to the Nolan principles, We think that all MPs should adhere to the Nolan principles. At the moment, we do not think that they follow them. We want all MPs to take an oath to follow the Nolan principles, and be scrutinised if they fail. We feel that there is a lack of public accountability at the moment.,

Close salary linked public sector pension schemes to new members, We urge the Government to close salary linked public sector pension schemes to new members, as we believe they hark back to when public sector pay was lower than private sector pay and was introduced to retain people in public service.,  We believe pay scales are now on parity and it is unjustifiable to maintain this.

We believe these schemes are financially unsustainable and a great cost to the British Taxpayer and should therefore be replaced with defined contribution pension schemes in line with the private sector.

Stop Religious Education (RE) being compulsory in English schools from Year 10, We urge the Government to stop making Religious Education (RE) compulsory in schools in England, and to allow it to be an optional subject from Year 10 onwards., Many schools make RE a compulsory GCSE. We believe children who are not interested in RE could have more choice and time to spend on subjects that they are interested in. A 2023 Ofsted reports showed that the quality of Religious Education in schools was of poor quality.

Retain the powers of local planning committees on building applications., We think removing local planning committees from the decision making process for building applications could mean local people have less of a say in what happens to their communities. Building is necessary but we feel the government's plans could affect small communities and access to services., We want the government to allow local councils to retain the power to decide when planning committees should grant or deny planning applications, but streamline the process, speed it up and give final decisions. Inform the public more openly in order to give them time to support or oppose.
 
Without this control, green belts could be swallowed up at an exponential rate, a process which may not be reversible.

New rules on internal exclusions and independent body to be established, We think removing children from classrooms, sometimes called "internal exclusion", is misused. We think the Government needs to replace current advice with definitive rules. Introduce an independent body where complaints about internal exclusion, detention, and other exclusion are reviewed., We think the excessive use of internal exclusion is having a detrimental effect on young people and limiting their education, frequently for the wrong reasons. Many children are fearful in school due to the sudden and volatile nature that detentions and internal exclusions are given. We think teachers are ill equipped or inexperienced so resort to bullish behaviours and the misuse of sanctions.
Schools need to be held to account.
Stop the closure of Abbey House Museum., Stop the closure of Abbey House Museum in Kirkstall.  And hopefully full fund it., Fund the museum. Through local or national funding

Reduce the home building targets to 200,000 houses per year., Lower national homebuilding targets to an achievable level for local councils, builders and infrastructure providers, rather than what we think are arbitrary numbers. We think changes in housing targets need to be in small, workable increments., Many local councils are very aware of the need for social and affordable housing. We think current target are not achievable under the current planning system. We think the present targets give developers too much control of housing provision but fail to deliver the houses needed. We think we do not have the labour force nor the material provision to deliver the housing targets put forward in the new NPPF. We think the present targets will not deliver the number of houses and leave local councils without any meaningful control.

Ban bonus payments and honours in all UK Government funded public bodies, Ban bonus payments and honours in the Civil service, all state schools all collages and universities, and all government departments and quangos.,

Tighten the regulations on electric vehicle charger providers, We would like the Government to introduce new national regulations: 
1. If a charger fails for any reason, the provider should  be fined for each non-functioning day
2. Providers would be compelled to offer contactless payment and be linked to national payment systems., We believe electric vehicle adoption is being held back by unreliable and unpredictable charging infrastructure. We feel the system is currently very chaotic - some chargers work only for those signed up to the network in question. Recent chargers are supposed to offer contactless payment, but this does not always work. We think failures at chargers are very common for a variety of payment and technical issues, without appropriate penalties.

I want the government to suspend all 'net zero' policies immediately., I want the government to suspend all policies relating to 'net zero' with immediate effect., The science behind 'net zero' is by no means settled (not that science ever can be, in any event). Renewable energy is costly, harmful to wildlife and itself has a huge negative environmental impact. Renewable energy is only economically viable with vast taxpayer subsidies which the country can ill afford. UK carbon emissions are trivial on a global scale. Germany has suffered massive economic damage in its own drive to pursue 'net zero' and if we do not act soon, the UK will follow suit.

Raise the expensive car supplement threshold to £50k, Raise the expensive car supplement, also known as the "luxury car tax" threshold from £40,000 to £50,000 to better reflect current car prices and help ensure fairness for ordinary buyers., We feel that the £40,000 threshold, set in 2017, no longer reflects modern car prices. 

We think many standard vehicles now fall within this range, unfairly subjecting ordinary families and individuals to additional taxes originally intended for high-end luxury cars. 

We believe raising the threshold to £50,000 would address this imbalance and would help prevent overtaxing regular buyers.

Ratify the Indigenous and Tribal Peoples Convention, 1989, We want the Government to ratify the Indigenous and Tribal Peoples Convention, 1989 (ILO convention 169). We believe the English, Scottish and Welsh are the indigenous peoples of Great Britain and should be recognised and protected as such., We believe DNA evidence shows that invasions of Britain over the last 2,000 years had less genetic impact than previously thought, and that the English, Scottish and Welsh are indigenous peoples. We want the Government to ratify the convention to provide recognition and protection.

Ban the use of private jets rather than putting additives in cow's food, Ban people from owning and using privates jets, which we think would replace the need for additives in cow feed to reduce their methane emissions., Private jets are an unnatural source of pollution compared to the natural process of cows farting and as many people protest about climate change so much we think private jets should be banned.

Create an Ecocide Prevention Act for England and Wales, This legislation would aim to protect the environment and its components - air, water, soil and biodiversity - from severe and deliberate widespread or long-term damage. This is to maintain the functioning of these valuable natural assets, and help meet climate and biodiversity targets., The environment contains many valuable resources for life on earth e.g. clean air to breath, clean water to drink, soil and pollinators for food, and natural habitats for climate change resilience. In 1997 one estimate put the global value of global ecosystem services at US$33 trillion per year (‘The value of the world's ecosystem services and natural capital’, Nature journal). A similar Bill has recently been proposed in the Scottish Parliament.

Give the Humanitarian Medal to all frontline ambulance staff for COVID response, We want the Government to issue the Humanitarian Medal to all frontline ambulance service personnel who served through the COVID 19 pandemic., We believe the eligibility criteria for the Humanitarian Medal has been met by any and all ambulance service personnel who actively responded to calls for help during the deadly COVID 19 pandemic, putting their and their families' lives at risk for the benefit of those who needed medical attention during the pandemic. We believe awarding a medal for their dedicated and selfless service and bravery would be a fitting reward.

Increase the UK Category B driving licence Maximum Authorised Mass to 4,500Kg, The Government should increase the MAM on a Category B driving licence to 4,500Kg. I believe the Department for Transport's proposal to raise the MAM for alternatively-fuelled vehicles is too complicated and will lead to anomalies & confusion for drivers with Category B entitlement., Many modern vehicles have lower payloads than older vehicles, because of new safety and emission requirements. An increase in MAM for Category B could lead to fewer vehicles on the road and increase productivity. It could also reduce Category C applications for drivers who have no intention of operating a lorry.

Make bank holidays for St George's Day in England and St David's Day in Wales, I think that these days should be bank holidays in England for St George's Day and Wales for St David's Day, to give children and workers the day off in order to socialise and celebrate these days. , Scotland and Northern Ireland have a bank holiday for their patron saints. I think that this would encourage traditionalism and nationalism for all the countries in the United Kingdom.

Ban councils putting council tax up higher than the 5% annual threshold , I want the Government to impose greater restrictions on councils putting council tax up by more the annual threshold of 5%. No increase above this should be allowed, with or without a referendum, without exception. , Council tax rates can be restricted by the government and councils should not be given any exemptions.

Launch a review on planning laws & Green Belt to increase housebuilding , As the country is failing to solve low homeownership, there must be a review into simplifying and clarifying planning processes, and reassessing and redefining the Green Belt, to increase housebuilding. , We believe that planning laws are outdated and complicated, including those in the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 and the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act. Hence, the Government needs to work urgently to identify and fix problems to ensure that there will be enough homes for younger generations to purchase in the future.

Ensure all petitions that have 100k signatures or more are debated in Parliament, It states on this website that "At 100,000 signatures, this petition will be considered for debate in Parliament" yet any petition that has garnered 100,000 signatures or more should DEFINITELY be debated in Parliament., Parliament and the Petitions Committee should realise that there is evident public interest in any petition that has achieved 100,000 or more signatures. Therefore, no 'considering' should occur and what needs to be implemented is that these petitions are debated regardless. 100,000 or more signatures clearly signifies that there is interest and MPs are paid more than enough to ensure that all these petitions are debated. No ifs or buts!

Rebate scheme for pensioners buying electric cars, I would like the Government to implement a rebate scheme for pensioners who buy electric cars. Many employed people have access to salary sacrifice schemes, so I think there should be an equivalent scheme for pensioners. , Pensioners should receive a rebate when they purchase an electric car. This might encourage greater use of electric cars and also be beneficial to pensioners, helping them to save money. I think pensioners would be keen to take advantage of such a scheme.

Don’t decommission HMS Westminster, Argyll, Bulwark & Albion and more RN funding, Media reports have said that these vessels may be axed from active service. We believe this must not happen and they should be maintained until there are sufficient replacements. It is also important that appropriate funds and personnel are allocated and maintained for the Royal Navy's (RN) upkeep., The government must adequately fund and maintain its commitment to defence and the UK's interests abroad. We believe that decommissioning and mothballing of four of the RN's vessels would diminish the UK’s ability to fulfil its commitments abroad and to maintain peace and order in the face of global tensions. We consider it is of paramount importance that the RN is well-funded and recruitment issues are addressed.

Introduce a Duty to Rescue Law in England and Wales, There is currently no statutory duty to rescue someone in need. Someone could openly watch an individual drown or be in serious peril, such as suffering an overdose or heart attack, and do nothing., In other countries, such as France and Spain there is a duty to rescue others. In France, under Article 223-6, those who fail to assist a person in danger is liable within the criminal courts and can be held accountable. In Spain, under Article 195, it is a criminal offence for a citizen to fail to provide or seek help to anyone in need so long as it does not endanger them. We think a duty to rescue should be enacted into the English and Welsh legal system.

Review the safety of electric buses, Recent reports of electric bus fires are causing concern over public safety., We feel it's time for the Government to investigate the causes of all electric bus fires and introduce any necessary measures to prevent them.
 
As bus companies use more and more electric vehicles we need to be confident that they are as safe as possible.

Reduce Vehicle Tax for cars aged between 20 and 40 years old, Under the current rules a car does not become exempt from Vehicle Tax until it is at least 40 years old. There are vehicles within the 20 to 40 year age bracket that are well loved, modern classics and without a reduction in tax, we may see these vehicles disappear from our roads., As the owner of a 20-year old modern classic, which is seldom driven more than a 1000 miles a year, I have just had my Vehicle Tax reminder though and even if I were to SORN the vehicle for 6 months of the year, it would still cost me £180 for 6 months. I like to take advantage of the occasional sunny day, year round, so I must pay £320 for this privilege. And there are owners of other models of the same car paying nearly £400 a year.

Promote circular fashion and educate the public about effects of fast fashion, We want VAT on the sale of second-hand goods abolished, import and export duties abolished, more education on the effects of fast fashion on the environment, and increased promotion of circular fashion., Fashion produces more CO2 than aviation and freight shipping combined, contributing to 10% of global carbon emissions. One organisation that reviewed the policies of 250 fashion brands found that 99% did not disclose a commitment to reduce the number of new items they produce. This must change.

Replace the Post Office with an independent not-for-profit body, We want the legislation governing the Post Office to be amended to replace the current Post Office with a new, independent, not-for-profit body that has more robust accountability mechanisms., We believe the Post Office is not fit for purpose, has lost the support of many of its users, and appears to have little concern for its employees or agents.
 
We want a new structure and leadership team to be established, which is more accountable to Parliament and the public.

Decriminalise abortion to protect rights of women and girls to access healthcare, Remove the Abortion Act 1967 to make all abortion safely accessible to all women and girls., At an extremely vulnerable time, women are facing the repercussions of an old, oppressive law which seeks to restrict necessary healthcare for women who do not wish to be pregnant.
 
By placing restrictions on women seeking abortions the law causes some women to carry out unsafe abortions at home. This can lead to a number of health complications for which they may be scared to seek attention for, for fear of prosecution.
 
Our law requires reform to reflect that of other modern nations, i.e. Canada.

Hold a referendum on repealing the Greater London Authority Act 1999, We believe that the GLA Act should be repealed and the Greater London Assembly dissolved as a result. The Government should hold a referendum asking the public if they want this to happen., We believe that the Mayor has far to much autonomy without being sufficiently held to account, and the Assembly has too limited powers.
 
Repealing the GLA Act could mean that TfL could be put under the control of the Department for Transport; and the Met Police and London Fire Brigade could be better aligned with national policing policies and structures. Other powers could be devolved to local councils with a way for them to liaise on related matters.

Require carbon footprint of items be printed on packaging, We would like legislation to be passed which requires manufacturers to print the carbon footprint of what they are selling on prominent places, for example on packaging., Achieving Climate Change targets requires that the average carbon footprint be reduced from around 10 tonnes to around 2 tonnes per head. However, at present consumers cannot make an informed decision at the point of purchase based on a clear statement of the carbon footprint of what they are buying. If consumers were properly informed (as they are on sugar content) then they would be able to make better decisions on how to reduce their footprint.

Ensure Government funding for police exceeds council tax police precept, It is within the power of Government and Parliament to set a framework where the majority source of police funding in England is from central government, rather than council tax. From 2024/2025, we want a funding formula that prevents the majority of police funding coming from council tax., From 03/2016 - 03/2024 the Council Tax precept increased by a percentage of 71%. Government funding increased by 29%. This year the precept  will increase by up to 7.6% vs 4.5% government funding. In the next spending review period several police areas may cross the point where Council Tax provides the majority of funding. We do not want this to happen. This could be achieved by limiting increases to the council tax precept for policing, or increasing central government funding.

Award Humanitarian Medal to everyone who helped during Covid-19, On 23 July 2023, the Government announced the introduction of a Humanitarian Medal. We believe it is a positive step that people will be recognised for their efforts in the future, but that people should be awarded this medal for past service during the pandemic., We think the creation of the Humanitarian Medal is fantastic moving forward but we feel it should be awarded retrospectively to those who have met its qualifying criteria prior to its creation. This should include His Majesty's Armed Forces, NHS staff and anyone who went above and beyond to assist during the Covid-19 pandemic.

Introduce a 50% reduction in council tax for Homes for Ukraine host families, We would like the Government to provide a 50% reduction in council tax for all households that are hosting Ukrainian families. We believe the reduction in council tax would ease the financial burden on host families, and could make it more feasible for them to provide assistance to those in need., By easing the financial burden, this reduction could encourage more families to participate in humanitarian efforts, fostering a culture of compassion and solidarity within communities. We believe it's a tangible way for the Government to support and incentivise acts of kindness and hospitality during times of crisis.

Help Stop Closure Of Holy Family Kidbrooke Primary School, Stop The Proposal For Closure That The Diocese Has Opted For And Look At Different Options Into Saving The School!

We Want To Protect The Well Being Of Our Students Aswell As Our Parents And Teachers

Give the UK people a Referendum on Net Zero, The UK Government to hold a Referendum on the UK aiming for Net Zero, with the option to Continue (for), or Stop (against) aiming for Net Zero., The Climate Change Committee (CCC) has said that reaching net zero would require net investments of £1.4 trillion by 2050.
 
This is a huge undertaking and massive investment for something the public hasn't directly voted on.
 
The UK's input to C02 is relatively small, and when facing massive political upheaval worldwide including potential wars, we believe any benefit of Net Zero is outweighed by the costs of achieving this.

Don’t make students who don’t get a level 4 in maths/English GCSE retake them , Don’t require students not achieving a level 4 to retake GCSE English or maths in post-16 education. Some students don’t want to and think it may not benefit them in their future career plans., Some people do not find the subjects such as English and maths interesting or find them difficult. If they did not have to study to resit them then they could focus their learning on something that interests them more and will benefit them in the future. For example, I believe it might be better for a trainee tradesman to not have to spend time studying for maths or English when they could be out learning in the real world to help them to get a job in the future.

Scrap the 2035 petrol and diesel car ban, We want the government to scrap the 2035 ban on the sale of new petrol and diesel cars., We do not think that electric vehicles are suitable for the majority. They can be expensive to buy, repair, insure and charge (using public chargers). Modern petrol and diesel cars do not pollute as much as they used to.

Allow blue badge holders to use personal electric vehicles on public land, For me and other disabled people, using an electric scooter or Segway is the only way to leave the house and have independence. However, we risk being fined and getting penalty points. Allow blue badge holders to use personal electric vehicles on public land after an assessment., I think there should be a law in place to make sure people are road worthy to keep other road users safe. I have tried a wheelchair, electric wheelchair and mobility scooter and have had issues with all of them. An electric scooter works perfectly for me and I know this is also the case for others. If this law was passed it I think it would change the lives of many people.

Increase funding to councils for pothole repairs and implement repair targets, I want the government to increase funding to local councils for pothole repairs. I also want the government to put in place strict repair targets that if councils fail to meet then council tax payers will be entitled to a rebate., The UK is thought to have more than one million potholes. Councils sometimes claim to not have enough funding to meet the repair demand. Roads can be left in a dangerous condition posing a high risk to network users, and impacting on our quality of life. I think the government needs to plug the funding gap and at the same time hold the council's to account by implementing strict repair targets that result in financial penalties, by way of a rebate to tax payers if they are not met.

Sever diplomatic ties with Russia, I want the UK to sever diplomatic ties with Russia., Because I have been on the ground in cities like Kherson and other cities that have been under attack, like Lviv and Odesa too.
 
During my volunteer work I have witnessed the daily struggle of Ukrainians.
 
I have seen evidence with my own eyes of destruction done to humanitarian and civilian infrastructure.
 
I have met civilians who are right now suffering at the hands of aggression. I believe we must sever diplomatic ties.

Ban the use of AI to generate media (eg. images, videos, voice recordings, etc), AI software can generate images very similar to how a human would draw an image themselves, and generate voice recordings that sound like natural human speech. I wish for the use of such technology to be banned., I wish for the Government to outlaw the use of AI-generated technology, as I am concerned that artists, musicians or voice actors face the possibility of being completely replaced by an AI. 

The Screen Actors Guild - American Federation of Television and Radio Artists (SAG-AFTRA) has agreed a deal was made allowing the use of AI-generated voices to be used in the video game medium, before, during or after final development. We are concerned this will mean that voice actors could fail to get a role due to AI.

Ban non-stun slaughter, In modern society, we believe more consideration needs to be given to animal welfare and how livestock is treated and culled., We believe non-stun slaughter is barbaric and doesn't fit in with our culture and modern-day values, and should be banned, as some EU nations have done.

In a landmark case, the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg has ruled that a ban on the ritual slaughter of animals without prior stunning does not violate the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR). The Court considered that the protection of public morals, to which Article 9 of the Convention referred was not indifferent to the living environment of individuals covered by its protection and in particular to animals. We believe this supports the request of this petition.

Repeal the Climate Change Act 2008 and Net Zero targets, We consider that Parliament must revoke The Climate Change Act 2008 and related Net Zero targets as since 2008 when the The Climate Change Act became law many hundreds of scientists up to the highest Nobel Laureate level have jointly declared "There is no climate emergency"., We believe the Climate Change Act 2008 and related Net Zero targets are both now in effect based on just one side of a two-sided scientific debate as we do not consider there to be a scientific consensus on the hypothesis of human emissions causing climate change. We consider that one side only of a two-sided scientific debate is not an acceptable basis for significant legislation that could have major impacts of the UK's economy and citizens. We want the issue of Climate Change to be reconsidered from scratch based on views and evidence from all sides.

Hold a national poll to pick an English National Anthem, Hold a national poll on what the people would like to see as an English National Anthem. The anthem can be determined based on this. Potential options could include popular English music that might be suitable as an anthem., England currently lacks its own anthem. Since England is its own cultural entity, and England takes part in many events independently, we believe an anthem for the people of the nation aside from that of the United Kingdom would increase national pride, and fully utilise our rich cultural heritage.

Hold referendums for any changes to current Human Rights and international laws, We demand the UK Government hold referendums on any changes to current Human rights and international laws, to ensure these actions reflect the will of the people. We believe this is necessary to respect democracy, international law and human rights., Given the decline in public trust and the absence of a direct democratic mandate for these decisions, we demand that the UK Government hold referendums on any such changes.

End policies that lessen farming land area, yield or viability, We believe that the UK's food security could be jeopardised by 'Green', 'Nature', 'Re-wilding, 'Net Zero' and 'Sustainable' polices that lead to farmland going permanently out of production, reduce the yield or impose other restrictions or costs., The UK only produces part of its food needs. We consider that repurposing any farmland for 'Green', 'Nature', Re-wilding, 'Net Zero' and 'Sustainable' policies can only increase our vulnerability to food insecurity. We consider that the agricultural viability and income of farms MUST be strongly protected, maintained and guaranteed in ALL 'Green', 'Nature' Re-wilding, 'Net Zero' & 'Sustainable' policies to safeguard ALL farming and farmers that produce food for us from farmland.

Increase threshold for extra tax on luxury cars to £50,000, I think the government needs to raise the threshold for paying more vehicle excise duty (VED) from a £40,000 to £50,000 car cost price. This could allow lower paid people to buy luxury vehicles and not penalise them with what we believe is an extortionate tax that has nothing to do with emissions., People might purchase the lower model of a car because of the surcharge. The luxury model might take them over the £40,000 threshold, even though it has exactly the same engine size. Increase it to £50,000 so it is paid by those buying more expensive cars. This could help people to purchase newer vehicles with more safety features like reversing cameras and better longer lasting seats like leather or leather alternatives. This might encourage them to keep the vehicle longer.
Declare St. David's Day a public holiday in Wales, I'm asking Parliament to consider declaring St. David's Day a public holiday in Wales.,

Require 'freezing' of non-physical assets of MPs while in office, This law will require all non-physical assets (for example: Stocks and Shares, Bank Accounts, Bonds, etc.) to be liquidated and kept in interest-free, government-monitored accounts. This law will only apply for the time that they are MP., Many political figures have dramatically increased their net worth during their times of great political influence. I believe that many decisions made by members of parliament could be swayed towards personal gain, increasing net worth and status instead of benefiting the public and improving the state of the country. This law could help prevent possible corruption and ensure decisions will be made for the benefit of the public and the country.

Seek to expel USA from the UN using Article 6 of the UN Charter, We believe the USA has persistently violated the principles of the UN Charter, both with and without its veto power, including by vetoing motions relating to Palestine, including calls for an immediate ceasefire., We want the Government to raise our voices and invoke Article 6 – to seek to expel the USA from the United Nations.
Article 6 allows for any member of the UN to be expelled – even if they sit on the Security Council – for persistently violating the principles of the United Nations. Expulsion under Article 6 is decided by the General Assembly upon the recommendation of the Security Council.
 
We believe the UN is in need of fundamental reform so it can properly and fairly represent the nations of the world and ensure global justice, peace and friendly relations between all peoples including, but not limited to the people of Palestine. We think expelling the USA from the UN is the first necessary step in this process.

Mandate robust safety posts at bus stops to prevent fatal accidents, My son Logan's death highlights the need for bus stop safety. We believe our loss and others affected by bus stop deaths could have been avoided by installing crash bollards. We want urgent action to prioritise pedestrian safety at stops, installing bollard and posts to prevent vehicle collisions.
, Too many lives are lost while people are standing at bus stops. People are waiting static at the side of busy roads. My son was trapped inside a bus stop shelter when a lorry hit him, he had nowhere to run. Protection posts could have saved his life. Others have died in the same way and I believe that this could have been avoided. We want to make it legislation that all relevant authorities must install mandatory posts at every bus stop to protect our children and citizens.

To make Anglophobia  a form of Hate Speech, To make  Anglophobia
 (from Latin Anglus "English" and Greek φόβος, phobos, "fear"), refers to opposition, dislike, fear, hatred, oppression, persecution, and discrimination of English people and/or England).

A Hate Speech and  thus a criminal offence., On the 7th day of the 7th Month the Terrorist Attack in Britain caused the largest loss of life from an act separate from War. 

It's roots lay in Anglophobia. Subsequent attacks in the UK have also been based around Anglophobia along with the desecration of War Memorials and national monuments.

People are afraid that their very presence and way of life are constantly being undermined by this form of discrimination.

Require dog owners to prevent off-lead dogs approaching on-lead dogs, We want the Government to make it a legal requirement for dog owners to prevent a dog which is not on a lead from approaching a dog which is on a lead, in a public place., If a dog is on lead, it is for a reason, and is being controlled by its owner. Some dogs are reactive and will defend their owners and themselves if threatened by an off lead dog. We believe that one owner saying "it's ok my dog is friendly" is absolutely not an excuse for one dog to invade another dog's space. A dog and its owner should be able to walk freely without fear of other dogs causing intimidation to them. If a dog is on lead it is on a lead for a reason - do not let other dogs approach it!

Provide funding so the NHS can prescribe wigs to all patients with Alopecia, Alopecia affects thousands of individuals in the UK. Although many NHS trusts offer wigs on prescription to cancer patients, many people with alopecia are unable to access them., Wigs are a source of help for Alopecia where many people simply cannot start to attempt to leave their homes without one. This is not a choice it is a necessity.
 
We want to see it as standard that every person should be able to access a wig from the NHS. This is not cosmetic it is an essential item of support for Alopecia patients.

Require microplastic filters on all new washing machines from 2027, We think the Government should mandate microplastic filters on all new washing machines from 2027. 700,000 microplastic fibres can be released in every clothes wash. We think action is needed!, We think that mandating microplastic filters on new washing machines is crucial. Evidence shows synthetic fibres from clothing are a source of microplastics in water bodies and can harm marine life, enter the human food chain, and our bodies. Filters can mitigate this by capturing microplastics before they are discharged into wastewater systems. Numerous studies have highlighted the effectiveness of these filters, and they should be built into washing machines as standard.

Require drivers to take a hazard perception test every 10 years, I would like the Government to introduce a mandatory hazard perception test every 10 years. This could be done when people renew their driving licence., On today's roads, too many people are getting hit and injured or killed on crossings as they cross because drivers are driving without due care and attention. Pedestrians have right of way at many crossings but all too often drivers are not seeing them. This could help improve the safety of people and enable Police attention to be diverted to other important matters.

Run a competition to commission an NHS logo which incorporates the George Cross, The Queen awarded the George Cross to the NHS in 2021.  We believe incorporating the award appropriately into the NHS logo will provide all NHS workers with a constant reminder of the high esteem their role is held by the nation., We think commissioning a national competition for an appropriate logo will remind the nation of the contribution of the NHS to society over many years. Given the nature of the award we believe Parliament is the best place to propose, debate and approve this initiative. There is historical precedent from a previous collective George Cross in the case of the flag of Malta.

Cut Mp salaries, There is a cost of living crisis! Mp should not have second homes they should not earn astronomical salaries. We need a people’s government! It’s time for a change., Save money but cutting fat cat salaries. Cut MP pay ! I would be an mp for 30,000 not 90,000

Provide additional funding for more bike lanes, We want more bike lanes for cyclists who need to get places, such as get to trails, or get to work. This could help reduce car use, and so carbon dioxide levels. This could also mean road cyclists have less fear of getting hit by a car and may feel more inclined to go on their bike., It could create a positive effect on the environment as more people may want to ride their bike, which could lead to less cars on the road. This could mean that less carbon dioxide will be emitted into the atmosphere. Cyclists may also be better able to ride without the fear of getting hit by a car.

Pay phlebotomists in NHS trusts across the UK, band 4 Agenda for change (AFC), Involve the Department of Health and social care, to implement a fixed pay banding (Band 4) for all phlebotomists who work within NHS trusts in the UK., Currently phlebotomists are being paid band 2 agenda for change. Due to rise in cost of living, and the increase in minimum wage, the current banding does not reflect the skills, knowledge, experience, or risks taken by phlebotomist when they perform their roles. A band 4 pay will boost morale, and improve working lives for phlebotomists across the nation. Otherwise, trusts will lose experienced phlebotomist who would otherwise work elsewhere for the same pay (less risk) if not more pay.

Stop the redesign of our Nationa flag, Make it illegal for any sports body to allow a change in the Nations individual fags and the Countries Union Flag., It feels like the FA are happy to allow a National Flag looking nothing like our St George’s Cross on our National strip because a manufacturer thinks it’s a modern twist! There should be no modern twist on any countries flag unless agreed by its population.

Change the English football team kit to include the cross of St George., I would like our government to realise it isn't illegal to be English, and recognise that we are all proud of our flag and what it represents., I think it is unacceptable that the FA and the corporate world can change a nations national flag without considering the implications on our national identity.

End the Badger Cull, To debate in parliament and hopefully put an end to what we see as the disastrous and inhumane badger culls that have been in place in England for over a decade, the new proposals for which could lead to significant reduction of the species across much of the country., The incumbent government has introduced a consultation on badger culls in our country. After saying in 2021 they would phase out this practice, the Government is now consulting on plans to allow it to continue.
Restore St George’s Cross On England Football Shirt, Don’t let our English culture fade. We should be proud… simple.,
Change England flag on back of the new kits back to St George Cross, Step in and sort it out, Disrespectful to our nation
