Review diplomatic relations with Hong Kong, The UK has engaged in diplomatic relations with Hong Kong representatives under the Vienna Convention of Consular Relations. In light of recent events, we want the Government to review diplomatic relations with Hong Kong., We are concerned that there is an ongoing erosion of Hong Kong's autonomy and rights, and that China is consistently violating the Sino-British Joint Declaration and disregarding the rule of law.
 
Following what we see as the death of the “One Country, Two Systems” principle we want the UK to review diplomatic relations with Hong Kong, including the diplomatic privileges held by the Hong Kong representatives in the UK.

Make it a legal requirement to list an expected salary on job advertisements, We think the Government should require recruiters to display the salary (or salary range) when advertising job listings, digitally or otherwise., Many recruiters are not doing this themselves. We think the Government should make this law, so the public can enjoy transparency, and the market could be slightly increased due to competitive beating.

Do not introduce Vehicle Excise Duty for zero emission cars, I would like plans to introduce Vehicle Excise Duty for zero emission cars to be withdrawn, as this may steer people away from getting an electric car and stop the government from reaching its zero emissions goal., We believe this change will not make this fairer as zero emission vehicle owners are helping the government achieve its zero emissions goal by paying a premium on these electric cars. Now the Government wants owners of zero emission vehicle to pay VED when their vehicles don't emit CO2? VED is based on CO2 emissions and we believe that cars that don't emit CO2 shouldn't have to pay VED. We think this will lead to more people using cars that burn fossil fuels for longer, and so cause greater harm to the environment. We also believe this could push people to leave the country to go to places with different tax regimes.

Make recommendations of pay awards bodies binding on Government, Pay rises for MPs are implemented automatically, and the Government appears to be sympathetic to pay increases for civil servants. Recommendations by other pay review bodies are often subject to delay, or not implemented in full. We want recommendations by all pay awards bodies to be binding., We want legislation enshrining the independence of pay review bodies in law, and making their recommendations binding on the Government, with pay increases implemented on the same day for all public sector workers for which there are pay review bodies. This would mean that, as with decisions by IPSA about pay for MPs, the Government would not be able to delay or adjust decisions by pay review bodies.

Reduce the minimum salary requirement for the New Skilled Workers route of 2024, Reduce the £38,700 per year salary threshold requirement for immigrants to obtain a job via the skilled workers route, which has been implemented in 2024., The minimum salary threshold has increased to £38,700; we believe this is unrealistic and impossible for many people. We are concerned it will have a significant impact on graduates as starting salaries at many companies are lower than this. We believe it is unfair and discriminatory when a person has been studying for 4-5 years, contributing to the country via tax and building relationships only to be forced to leave if they cannot find a job with a salary above the minimum threshold. Thus, we believe it should be reduced.

Require elected representatives and public servants use zero emission travel, The aim is Net Zero by 2050. But targets have been delayed for BEV and heat pumps already. We want the Government to lead by example and introduce new requirements for others by passing legislation to require elected representatives and public servants use zero emission travel., In the face of a Climate Emergency we want the Government to do more to show the problem is real and they are tackling it urgently. To this end we want legislation to be passed as soon as possible to ensure that all elected representatives and public servants, including members of the Cabinet, Civil Service Heads, all City Mayors, police officers must travel within the UK and Europe using only zero emissions transport.

Allow Ukrainians working in the UK and not receiving benefits to apply for ILR, Let Ukrainians who came to the UK under the Ukrainian scheme apply for ILR if they never applied for any benefits and work full time., The war in Ukraine continues, and nobody knows when it will stop. The extension of the Ukrainian scheme is very good and appreciated, but people still don't know what is next. Without the extension of the scheme, many Ukrainians may feel they have no choice but to apply for asylum. A scheme that allows Ukrainians who have been living and working in the UK, and not claimed benefits, to apply for ILR, would give security to a lot of really hardworking people.

Make councils accountable to the 2014 legislation on ehcps., I am calling for a reform on the current system which has become outdated and overstretched. 

Legal deadlines are not being met by LA’s with no accountability for this.


Children with disabilities have a right, by your law, to an education, one that is fit for purpose NOT fit for statistics!, The councils are not being held accountable for their failings and this needs to change! 


Wait times for appeals should be within weeks not months to years! 

Reform the ehcp system so that all children get a suitable education in a reasonable time when needs are identified. Increase funding and hold councils accountable to the law.

Extend the £2 Bus Fare Cap after December 2024, I want the Government to extend the £2 bus fare cap to ensure continued access to affordable transportation. I believe this initiative has proven to be beneficial for the community by facilitating mobility, reducing carbon emissions, and promoting social inclusion., I think the £2 bus travel scheme is vital for social inclusion, environmental sustainability, and economic growth. Providing affordable transportation, could improve access to essential services, reduce carbon emissions, and stimulate economic activity, benefiting individuals and communities alike.

Hold a referendum on leaving the European Convention on Human Rights, We call upon the Government to hold a referendum on leaving the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR). We believe the people should be given a say.
 
, We believe the Brexit referendum made it clear that we do not want judgments and rulings that have no democratic mandate. We think the ECHR continues to undermine parliamentary sovereignty and our democratic processes. We believe the time has come to give the people their say on our membership of the ECHR.
 
Give the people an in/out referendum on membership of the ECHR.

Make St. George's Day a Bank Holiday for England to celebrate it's patron saint., St. George's Day, celebrated on April 23rd, is the patron saint of England. It should be a bank holiday in England to allow people to celebrate national identity, inclusivity and culture. Like other countries have holidays for their patron saints. It could boost the economy with increased spending., Studies have shown that a significant portion of the population in the UK feels more connected to their regional identity rather than a unified British identity. Additionally, ongoing debates around issues like Brexit, Scottish independence, and the monarchy reflect the complexities within the UK regarding national identity. This can be seen in the rise of nationalist movements in Scotland and Wales, including concerns on the impact of globalization on traditional British values and culture.

Reduce delays for getting driving licence back after medical suspension, I would like people to sign this petition to call on the Government to increase the speed of the DVLA process for considering applications for a driving licence following a medical condition. Many people are experiencing enormous delays to get their license back after a medical suspension., I had my licence taken away for 12 months from 1st February 23 and 15 months later and after many calls, emails etc with the DVLA still nothing seems to be happening.
 
I have decided to form this petition because it appears that there are many drivers in the same position as me.

Require planning permission and public consultation to fell any tree, We believe current protections for trees, including Tree Preservation Orders (TPOs) are insufficient. We believe rules for felling trees should be amended to more closely reflect planning rules for property development., I want the Government to place the same protections on changes to trees as there are on other major changes to a property, including planning permission and a requirement for public consultation. We think that most important is a consultation phase where the changes being made are clearly laid out and objections can be raised.

Introduce a Magna Carta Day public holiday for England on 15 June, Institute a new national holiday for England. This should be a bank holiday, and would be on 15th June, the day in 1215 when Magna Carta was signed, which was a giant step towards English democracy., My suggestion is to have a public holiday on 15th June for Magna Carta Day. It's not a patron saint's day, so it's not religious, it's properly English, is important to our democracy, and has influenced other countries in one way or another, and it's in the summer!

Reverse the decision to allow Ofsted one-word judgements to remain., We want the Government to reverse this decision and abolish one-word overall judgements. We believe that they are harmful and misleading., In January a report from the cross-party Education Select Committee called for an alternative to the current single-word overall judgements. The government rejected the Select Committee's recommendation and ignored coroner’s concerns raised in a Prevention of Future Deaths report and raised by education professionals. We don't believe that they sufficiently quantified what the significant benefits are linked to single word judgements for schools or parents.

Provide a pedestrian/school crossing to outside of the school on the main road, Create a crossing to improve the safety of the children crossing in the area as it is a main road and there have been many incidents and close calls for children not being able to see around the corner when cars approach fast by the school., The school does not have the funds to be able to hire a lollipop person or anyone to help with pedestrian crossing. By putting a zebra crossing or child friendly area to cross this would reduce risk and families in the area would feel more safe.

Require MPs to evidence all contributions in Parliament and introduce penalties, I think that MPs should be required to substantiate claims/statements made in Parliament. This could help ensure that MPs prioritise evidence based decisions, ensuring integrity and credibility by requiring independent, unbiased, peer-reviewed scientific evidence for all parliamentary contributions., All Members of Parliament to be mandated to substantiate all claims, speeches, statements, and actions with independent, unbiased, and peer-reviewed evidence from reputable academic sources prior to their contributions. Citing sources for every statement, speech, and action to be mandatory. Penalties for non-compliance: 1st breach - 3 months of suspension from Parliamentary activities, 2nd breach - 6-month suspension, 3rd breach - 1-year suspension.

Ensure every Jobcentre has a private room for interviews by the end of 2024, A recent freedom of information request to the DWP confirmed that only 30% of job centres have private rooms available., At a minimum we want every Jobcentre to have a private interview room, in order to provide privacy and dignity to service users.
 
Jobcentres are often set up with an 'open office' layout, where it can be possible to overhear conversations and personal details from other service users.
 
This does not seem appropriate for sensitive conversations, especially those that involve details of trauma, disability, mental health or past abuse.
 
Private rooms could enable claimants to feel safe to discuss their circumstances, without other people listening in and help preserve their dignity.
 
Every Jobcentre should have a private interview room.
